Episodes and terminal states

Many tasks end: a game is won or lost, a maze is escaped. Each run from start to end is an episode, and the state where it ends is terminal. Once there, nothing more happens and the return stops adding up.

Lesson 18's icy world (slip 0.2, $-1$ per move, $+10$ for 🏁, $-10$ for 🕳️). Now 🏁 and 🕳️ can end the episode.

The maths

In an episodic task each episode ends at some time $T$, when the agent enters a terminal state. The return from step $t$ adds the rewards up to the end, discounted by $\gamma$ (Lesson 4):

$$\begin{aligned} G_t &= R_{t+1} + \gamma R_{t+2} + \dots + \gamma^{T-t-1} R_T \\ &= \sum_{k=t+1}^{T} \gamma^{k-t-1} R_k \end{aligned}$$

$T$ is random: it depends on the slips and on the actions. It can differ from episode to episode.

Splitting off the first reward gives the recursion every later lesson is built on:

$$G_t = R_{t+1} + \gamma\, G_{t+1}, \qquad G_T = 0$$

The return now is the next reward plus the discounted return from the next step. At the end there is nothing left to collect.

One formula for both kinds of task. Treat the terminal state as absorbing: it moves only to itself, with reward 0. Then every episode goes on forever, and the extra rewards add nothing (the grey rows in the log). So episodic and continuing tasks share one definition (S&B §3.4):

$$G_t = \sum_{k=t+1}^{\infty} \gamma^{k-t-1} R_k$$

This allows $\gamma = 1$ when episodes always end, or $T = \infty$ when $\gamma < 1$, but not both. With rewards bounded by $R_{\max}$ and $\gamma < 1$ the sum is at most $R_{\max}/(1-\gamma)$. With $\gamma = 1$ and no end, it can grow without limit.

Untick "terminal" and put the robot on 🏁 with the route policy: it bumps into the edge and collects $+10$ again and again, which is Lesson 18's flaw. Its return is finite only because $\gamma < 1$. Set $\gamma = 1$ and it grows without bound.
